subject: mantisfly
title: Baby Mantisflies Ride Spiders, Drink Their Blood, Then Eat Their Eggs

scenes.text: Its babies hatch hungry, and their food is guarded by a spider.
It's a mantisfly: the front half of a praying mantis on lacewing wings.
Its tiny larvae climb onto a passing hunting spider and ride along.
Until she lays eggs, a larva drinks the spider's blood to stay alive.
When she spins her egg sac, it slips inside, gets sealed in with the eggs, and eats them.
So the spider guards her nursery, with the egg thief locked inside.

description:
Mantisfly larvae hitch a ride on hunting spiders and wait for them to lay eggs.
Until then, a larva feeds on the spider's blood. When the spider builds her egg sac, it slips inside and eats the eggs.
Would you have guessed this insect starts life as a spider's passenger?
first_comment: A larva riding a male spider can switch to the female when they mate. Which is creepier: the ride or the egg sac?
